cards: Mahatma Gandhi was the leader of the Indian independence movement, known for his strategy of non-violent mass resistance.
Benito Mussolini was an Italian politician who founded Fascism and ruled Italy as dictator from 1922 until 1943.
Vladimir Lenin was a Russian revolutionary who led the Bolshevik party.
Mao Zedong was a founding member of the Chinese Communist Party who led the Chinese Soviet Republic in Jiangxi and emerged as party leader during the Long March of 1934–1935.
Joseph Stalin (1878–1953) was the leader of the Soviet Union from the late 1920s until his death.
Adolf Hitler was the leader of the Nazi Party and dictator of Germany from 1933 to 1945.
Mikhail Gorbachev (1931–2022) was the last leader of the Soviet Union, general secretary of the Communist Party from 1985 and president from 1990 to 1991.
Mustafa Kemal Atatürk was an Ottoman army officer who led the Turkish national movement after the First World War and became the founding president of the Republic of Turkey.
Kwame Nkrumah was the leader of the Gold Coast's independence movement and the first prime minister and president of Ghana, which became independent in 1957.
Woodrow Wilson was President of the United States from 1913 to 1921, who led the country into the First World War in 1917.
Franklin D. Roosevelt was an American Democratic politician who served as the 32nd president of the United States from 1933 until his death in 1945, the only president elected four times.
Haile Selassie was the last Emperor of Ethiopia, who died in 1975.
Gamal Abdel Nasser was an Egyptian army officer who led the Free Officers' coup of 1952 and became president of Egypt in 1956.
Julius Nyerere was a Tanzanian teacher and politician who led the Tanganyika African National Union to independence in 1961.
Suharto was an Indonesian army general who took power after the failed coup of 1965, during mass killings of alleged communists, and was president from 1967 to 1998.
B. R. Ambedkar was an Indian jurist, economist and social reformer who chaired the drafting committee of the Constitution of India.
Charles de Gaulle was a French general and statesman who led the Free French during the Second World War and later founded the Fifth Republic, serving as president from 1959 to 1969.
Victor Emmanuel III was King of Italy from 1900 to 1946.
Frederick Lugard was a British colonial administrator who became high commissioner of the Protectorate of Northern Nigeria in 1900.
Jawaharlal Nehru was a leader of the Indian National Congress in the struggle for independence and a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi, imprisoned many times by the British.
Nelson Mandela was a South African anti-apartheid leader born into a junior branch of the Thembu royal house.
Sukarno was the leader of the Indonesian independence movement and the first president of Indonesia.
Xi Jinping is a Chinese politician who has been general secretary of the Chinese Communist Party since 2012 and president of the People's Republic of China since 2013.
Francisco Franco was a Spanish general who rose in the colonial wars in Morocco.
Ronald Reagan was the 40th president of the United States, serving from 1981 to 1989, after careers as a film actor and governor of California.
Bảo Đại was the last emperor of the Nguyễn dynasty of Vietnam, reigning under French protection from 1926.
Sun Yat-sen was a Chinese revolutionary and founder of the Kuomintang (Nationalist Party).
Winston Churchill was a British statesman and Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1940 to 1945 and 1951 to 1955, leading Britain through the Second World War.
Augusto Pinochet was a Chilean general who led the military coup of 11 September 1973 that overthrew Salvador Allende.
Deng Xiaoping was a Chinese communist revolutionary who was the paramount leader of the People's Republic of China from 1978 until the early 1990s.
Hugo Chávez was a Venezuelan army officer who led a failed coup in 1992 and was elected president in 1998.
Clement Attlee was a British Labour politician and prime minister of the United Kingdom from 1945 to 1951.
Donald Trump (born 1946) is an American businessman and Republican politician who served as the 45th president of the United States from 2017 to 2021 and became the 47th president in January 2025.
Ho Chi Minh was a Vietnamese revolutionary who helped found the French Communist Party and the Indochinese Communist Party, and in 1941 formed the Viet Minh.
Jorge Luis Borges was an Argentine writer whose short-story collections Ficciones (1944) and The Aleph (1949), with their labyrinths, mirrors and imaginary books, made him one of the most…
Martin Luther King Jr. was an American Baptist minister and the best-known leader of the civil rights movement.
Max Weber was a German sociologist, historian, jurist and political economist, one of the central figures in the development of sociology.
Milton Obote was Uganda's first prime minister at independence in 1962 and later its president.
Wilhelm II was the last German Emperor and King of Prussia, reigning from 1888 until his abdication in 1918.
Alfred Milner was a British colonial administrator who as high commissioner for southern Africa from 1897 pressed the Transvaal into the Second Boer War.
